Explain how a VPN works in simple words
8:33 PM

A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and the internet. Everything you send goes through it, locked so nobody in the middle can read it.

Here is how it goes:

Your device locks (encrypts) your data before it leaves.
The locked data travels to the VPN company's computer.
That computer unlocks it and sends it on to the website, so the website sees the VPN's address, not yours.
The reply comes back the same way.

Why people use it: safer on public Wi-Fi, and your internet provider can't see which sites you visit. What it doesn't do: it won't stop viruses or hide you from sites you sign in to. You are just trusting the VPN company instead of your provider.
